items.title: 10.17.2 Feasibility of a reaction using E standard values

source_refs.note: Topic 10.17.2 with Figures 10.9 and 10.10, printed pages 231-233. Sign and value slips in the printed E cell calculations are noted.

blocks.text: Standard electrode potential values measure how easy or difficult it is to oxidise or reduce a species. The values are listed in order of increasingly negative values, with the more oxidised form on the left and the more reduced form on the right of each half-equation. The more positive the E standard, the greater the tendency of the half-equation to proceed forward and the easier it is to reduce the species on the left; the less positive the E standard, the greater the tendency to proceed in reverse and the easier it is to oxidise the species on the right.

To check the feasibility of a reaction between Mg2+ and Ag we need the half-equations: Mg2+ + 2e- giving Mg, E standard = -2.32 V, and Ag+ + e- giving Ag, +0.80 V. If Mg2+ were reduced and Ag oxidised, E cell = E(reduction) - E(oxidation) = (-2.32) - (+0.80) = -1.52 V; the negative value shows the reaction is not feasible. The reaction between Ag+ and Mg is feasible, since E cell = (+0.80) - (-2.32) = +1.52 V is positive.

For the Cu2+/Cu and Zn2+/Zn pair, zinc has the greater tendency to lose electrons, so the reaction in that half-cell runs in reverse, Zn giving Zn2+ + 2e-, and the two half-equations combine to Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) giving Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s), the reaction taking place in the cell: zinc metal with copper ions is feasible, and if the forward reaction is feasible the reverse (copper metal with zinc ions) is not. A piece of copper placed in 1.00 mol dm-3 Zn2+ solution does not react. With the half-equations written one above the other, the direction of reaction follows a clockwise pattern (reactant, product, reactant, product) starting from the top left (Figure 10.10): a reaction occurs so that the stronger oxidising agent reacts with the stronger reducing agent.

blocks.alt: Two half-reactions in a box: Cu2+ + 2e- = Cu at +0.34 V above Zn2+ + 2e- = Zn at -0.76 V. Cu2+ at the upper left, the better oxidant, is turned into Cu; Zn at the lower right, the better reductant, is turned into Zn2+. Curved arrows go round clockwise, giving Cu2+ + Zn -> Cu + Zn2+.
blocks.caption: A reaction goes in the direction in which the stronger oxidant and reductant react (clockwise pattern) (original diagram after Figure 10.10).
